title: Mechanical Compatibility, Pre-Intervention Content Binding and Provenance Direction: A Synthetic F0–F5 Audit — BIT-REALITY-KNOWLEDGE-001
abstract: English abstract This report archives the terminal audit of BIT-REALITY-KNOWLEDGE-001, separating mechanical compatibility, temporal evidence and knowledge-provenance direction. In a locked synthetic two-model sled fixture, a prescribed post-load velocity interval is compatible with M_coast and excludes M_comp. This is a model-class result, not an identification of a unique real-world mechanism. A late verified receipt does not establish a pre-intervention prediction. Independent pre-intervention seals support the control workflow only under declared fixture assumptions. The F3 audit preserves a false acceptance by the historical F2 implementation when two differently named stores share effective editing authority. An external immutable anchor W binds the D/S content pair before intervention under synthetic trust assumptions, but does not establish that A and B were separately sealed in the required order. Two histories with the same accessible record retain different sealing-order truths; P_SHARED+W therefore remains HOLD_LOCK_ORDER and HOLD_DIRECTION. Mathematics-to-physics and physics-to-mathematics labels concern each branch's evidence chronology, not a claim that mathematics causes physical laws. No actual sled measurements, real timestamp verification, real anchors, general theorem or novelty priority is established. The supplement preserves the prelock note, F0–F4 reports and F5 DOCX unchanged, including embedded historical code and negative results. REL-001 performs archive integrity and publication preparation only; it does not rerun scientific checks or reopen F0–F5. Tóm tắt tiếng Việt Báo cáo lưu trữ kiểm toán terminal BIT-REALITY-KNOWLEDGE-001, giữ riêng tương thích cơ học, chứng cứ thời gian và hướng nguồn gốc tri thức. Trong fixture xe trượt tổng hợp với hai mô hình đã khóa, khoảng vận tốc sau tải được stipulate tương thích với M_coast và loại M_comp; kết quả không xác lập cơ chế duy nhất của thế giới. Biên nhận hậu ký không chứng nhận dự báo trước can thiệp. Đối chứng niêm phong độc lập chỉ hỗ trợ hướng quy trình theo giả định fixture. Kiểm toán F3 bảo toàn lỗi false accept của mã F2 lịch sử khi hai kho khác tên cùng quyền sửa có hiệu lực. Bản neo ngoài W ràng buộc cặp nội dung D/S trước can thiệp theo các giả định tin cậy tổng hợp, nhưng không xác minh A rồi B được khóa riêng. Hai lịch có cùng hồ sơ đọc được vẫn có sự thật thứ tự khóa khác nhau; P_SHARED+W tiếp tục HOLD_LOCK_ORDER và HOLD_DIRECTION. Các nhãn Toán→Lý và Lý→Toán chỉ thuộc lịch chứng cứ của từng nhánh. Không có phép đo xe, timestamp hay bản neo thật; tính mới và định lý tổng quát chưa được xác lập. Phụ lục giữ nguyên byte bản prelock, báo cáo F0–F4 và DOCX F5, kể cả mã lịch sử và kết quả âm. REL-001 chỉ kiểm toàn vẹn và chuẩn bị công bố, không chạy lại kiểm khoa học hoặc mở lại F0–F5. Existing third-party notices and terms remain applicable. Historical F0–F5 bytes and scientific verdicts are unchanged.

title: Multi-Level Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient reinforcement learning for safety-constrained trajectory optimization of collaborative industrial robots
abstract: Collaborative robots operating in modern manufacturing environments require trajectory planning strategies that simultaneously support efficiency, adaptability, and operational safety. This study proposes a Multi-Level Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (ML-DDPG) framework for safety-constrained trajectory optimization. The framework combines a strategic waypoint level, a continuous DDPG motion-control policy, and a reactive feasibility projection that corrects unsafe actions before execution. The trajectory-planning problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process with reward terms for goal progress, obstacle clearance, smoothness, energy, execution time, and safety. Descriptive experiments in a custom PyTorch-based three-dimensional environment compare ML-DDPG with conventional planners and the DDPG, TD3, and SAC baselines. In the retained single training run, ML-DDPG produced observed values of 98.7% success, 1.08 mm trajectory error, a 0.98 smoothness index, and no recorded collision. These values are single-run observations and are not means over independent seeds; variability and statistical significance cannot be estimated from the available record. The exported traces show faster reward growth within the 200-episode budget, and the single-run ablation record associates the largest observed gains with the combined multi-level, reward, and projection components. One UR5e demonstration yielded 0.018 m mean tracking error, 0.042 m maximum tracking error, and no collision in that trial. A separate ABB welding sequence is included only as qualitative feasibility evidence because synchronized trajectory, force, and weld-quality logs were unavailable. The findings motivate further evaluation, while multi-seed training, repeated hardware trials, complete reporting of evaluation procedures, and cross-platform validation remain necessary before broader generalization.

title: РАЗРАБОТКА МЕТОДА И АЛГОРИТМОВ АДАПТИВНОГО ФЕДЕРАТИВНОГО ОБУЧЕНИЯ С УЧЕТОМ РАСПРЕДЕЛЕННОГО ЗАПАЗДЫВАНИЯ КЛИЕНТСКИХ ОБНОВЛЕНИЙ
abstract: При федеративном обучении с неоднородными клиентскими данными и переменными задержками запоздавшие обновления могут ухудшать качество модели, а обмен параметрами с глобальным сервером увеличивает сетевую нагрузку. Целью исследования является разработка и теоретико-экспериментальное обоснование метода и алгоритмов адаптивного федеративного обучения с учетом распределенного запаздывания клиентских обновлений. Для обоснования разрабатываемых решений использованы событийная и непрерывная модели градиентных обновлений, спектральный анализ устойчивости, вероятностные оценки возраста и расхождения обновлений, а также оценка изменения градиента по кривизне функции потерь. Получены характеристическое уравнение и условие определения критического шага обучения. Разработан метод с выбором шага обучения и числа локальных шагов, оценивающий применимость запаздывающих обновлений. Предложены алгоритмы иерархического агрегирования с проверкой совместимости результатов и инкрементального дерева решений с раздельной адаптацией параметров и структуры. Вычислительные сравнения подтвердили сокращение передачи данных при выполнении ограничений качества и эффективность отбора обновлений. Поэтапным отключением компонентов оценен их вклад в качество обучения и ресурсные затраты. Полученные результаты подтверждают применимость решений при переменных задержках в условиях неоднородности клиентских данных.

title: Artificial Intelligence Model’s assessment of intra-sample heterogeneity of HER2 IHC in breast cancer is related to interobserver and intraobserver agreement among pathologists
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate assessment of HER2 status in breast cancer has been critical for guiding therapy and has become even more important with the emergence of antibody-drug conjugates, now also indicated in HER2-low tumors. However, inter- and intraobserver variability limits the reproducibility of HER2 IHC scoring among pathologists, particularly at the lower end of the expression spectrum. Artificial intelligence (AI) models offer potential to standardize and improve diagnostic accuracy and bring new insights into current practices shortcomings. Methods We conducted a study recruiting generalist and specialist pathologists from Rede D’Or centers across Brazil to assess digitized HER2 IHC whole slide images. The same images were presented for the pathologists with the interval of one month and to the AIM-HER2 (PathAI ®, Boston, MA) AI model. Intra- and interobserver agreement, as well as concordance with AI, were measured across 126 breast cancer samples. The association between sample features and agreement metrics was also analyzed using AI spatial breakdown data. Results Among 34 pathologists, median intraobserver concordance was 67.68% and median concordance with AI was 60.8%. Median interobserver agreement was 67.65%, with high agreement (> 85%) in 25.4% of samples. Significant positive correlations were observed among all agreement metrics. Samples with lower intra-sample heterogeneity, as determined by AI spatial breakdown scores, were associated with higher agreement levels. Conclusions Our findings highlight significant variability in HER2 IHC scoring among pathologists. AI models such as AIM-HER2 can be used to increase reproducibility of analysis and also to indicate the most difficult samples that can result in diagnostic discordance. We found that AI assessed intra-sample heterogeneity is correlated with a lower agreement rate among pathologists.

Samples with lower intra-sample heterogeneity, as determined by AI spatial breakdown scores, were associated with higher agreement levels. title: Exploring the Latent Structure of AMD Severity Using Retinal Foundation Models
abstract: Retinal foundation models have demonstrated strong performance across a wide range of ophthalmic tasks, yet relatively little is known about how disease-related information is represented within their learned embeddings and whether this distribution influences downstream prediction performance. In this work, we use Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) as a case study to investigate how disease severity is represented within the embedding space of RET-CLIP, a retinal vision-language foundation model, using bilateral fundus images from the AREDS dataset, benchmarked against non-retinal encoders. We first characterize the distribution of AMD severity within the learned representation space and then evaluate how this structure influences classification performance across three clinically relevant task formulations of increasing granularity. Finally, we analyze the most influential latent dimensions combining feature attribution, statistical phenotype association, and qualitative image analyses. Our results show that RET-CLIP represents AMD severity as a continuous spectrum rather than a set of discrete categories, with healthy and advanced disease stages exhibiting clearer separation than intermediate ones. This organization was reflected in downstream performance, which decreased from a balanced accuracy of 0.844 and 0.814 for binary AMD and Late-AMD detection respectively to 0.446 for six-class grading. Furthermore, the most influential latent dimensions were statistically associated to distinct retinal phenotypes, including drusen accumulation, pigmentary alterations, and advanced retinal lesions. These findings suggest that the structure of retinal foundation-model representations influences the difficulty of clinically relevant prediction tasks and demonstrate the potential of representation-level analysis for understanding disease organization and improving interpretability.

title: How Should We Evaluate Naturalness for Synthetic Speech with a Foreign Accent?
abstract: Recent advances in speech synthesis technology have enabled the generation of speech with diverse characteristics. One such characteristic is a foreign accent. In our preliminary experiments, we found that UTMOS, a widely used automatic speech quality assessment system, tended to assign lower scores to speech with stronger foreign accents, even though it is produced by a human speaker. This observation raised a question: How do humans evaluate the naturalness of foreign-accented speech? We conducted a large-scale subjective evaluation involving both native and non-native listeners under different evaluation instructions. The results showed that humans also considered accentedness when evaluating naturalness, but that defining naturalness in terms of human-likeness and selecting raters who have greater exposure to the target accent may enable more appropriate evaluation. This study aims to provide a starting point for future discussions on fairer and more appropriate evaluation of synthetic speech with a foreign accent.

title: The Moment Ladder: Exact Integer Checksums that Certify, Locate, and Fill
abstract: A string of digits, a frame, a tile of a matrix product, any list of integers, carries a ladder of exact totals: the plain sum T, the position-weighted sum W, the quadratic sum Q, the cubic C, and onward. This paper states the laws of that ladder and proves them by algebra and by exhaustive computation. Each rung stamps damage with an exact integer signature. The first m totals cannot all be silenced by a change touching at most m cells, which is the ladder theorem, a Vandermonde argument in plain integers, and the same argument read the other way fills m holes at known positions exactly. One wrong cell names itself: T is the error, W/T the position, Q = T·c² the confirmation, and with the quadratic rung the named cell is unique. Two or three wrong cells on a line are solved by the Prony recurrence in exact integers. The identity behind every use is linear: the ladder of a matrix product is predicted from its inputs, row moments of A·B equal A·(B·w) for any fixed weight vector w, so the columns may carry any fixed sign pattern without changing a theorem, and splitting an index into residue classes gives independent witness families that are the Chinese-remainder box of the ring seen on a tile. On the Fibonacci 60-ring the ladder is the ring's own arithmetic. The split Lucien Khan noticed in 2013, the sixty digits summing to 280 with the first thirty at 128 and the second thirty at 152, is its zeroth rung, the ring's constants 280, 8,760 and 344,660 repair all 540 single-digit corruptions with no reference copy, and every ring of the shell family carries the same stamps with its own half-period. On the ring itself one struck digit is already named by its rectangle, the twin grid of the system paper, with no total consulted, and the smallest damage that keeps every rectangle relation, a swap on all four corners, is stamped by W on the even rectangles and by Q on the odd ones. Every law is re-verified by enumeration when this document is built, and every number quoted from a companion paper is checked against that paper's archived record. The architectures built on these laws, frames, the fractal tower, the cube, the compute guard and the training guard, are the companion paper The Self-Healing Tower. How much they repair, and why, is the companion paper The Scaling Law.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI THEORY OF NEUROMORPHIC SILICON PHOTONIC INTELLIGENCE Unifying Chip Physics, Optical Computing, and Algorithmic Cognition for the Post-Electronic Era
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Neuromorphic Silicon Photonic Intelligence unifies silicon photonics, neuromorphic engineering, and algorithmic cognition to overcome von Neumann and thermodynamic bottlenecks. It proposes the Photonic Neural Silicon Chip (PNSC), executing deep learning matrix multiplications at light-speed via integrated interferometers. To ensure analog precision, it employs Noise-Aware Training, injecting hardware noise into digital backward passes. Scalability is achieved through WDM broadcast-and-weight topologies (O(N) footprint) and athermal tuning to eliminate parasitic power. Central is the Silicon Photonic Intelligence Index: SPII=(P×A×C×T)/[(P×A×C×T)+D×E+ε]. Under the Weakest-Link Axiom, it proves photonic intelligence requires simultaneous optimization of photonic, algorithmic, integrative, and thermodynamic dimensions. Guided by the Asymptotic Perfection Principle (max ~0.9901, reflecting the Landauer limit), it provides a definitive blueprint for sustainable, light-speed AI.

title: dnalang-core 0.3.0: circuit lineage on the run ledger
abstract: dnalang-core is a small language (dna::}{::lang) and toolchain for writing quantum circuits as genomes, evolving them, and running them with a hash-chained ledger written before every hardware submission. Version 0.3.0 records circuit lineage on that ledger: each generation of an evolutionary search appends, for every genome, the operator that produced it, its parents, its fitness and optionally its compiled circuit's SHA-256; hardware candidates are recorded as proposed, with their surrogate score, before submission; dnalang trace-lineage walks a genome's ancestry and refuses a ledger whose chain does not verify. Recording does not change the search. The ledger module is unchanged from 0.2.0. Verified: 36 tests pass and ruff is clean on Python 3.12, offline, on the released tree. Python 3.10 and 3.11 were not run. Version 0.2.0 was deposited as a snapshot inside 10.5281/zenodo.23087554.

title: Design and Implementation of a Telegram-Based Conversational AI Agent for Automated Personal Expense Management Using Large Language Models and Google Sheets
abstract: Manual logging of day-to-day personal expenses is often abandoned by users because it requires them to open a dedicated spreadsheet or application and enter data in a rigid, structured format. This paper presents the design and implementation of a conversational Artificial Intelligence (AI) agent that allows a user to record and retrieve personal expenses simply by chatting in natural language through the Telegram messaging platform. The system is built using the n8n low-code automation platform and combines a Telegram Trigger node, an AI Agent powered by an OpenAI Chat Model, a Simple Memory module for conversational context, and two Google Sheets tools, namely Read Expenses and Add Expense, that allow the agent to write new expense records to, and retrieve existing records from, a connected Google Sheet. When a user sends a message such as "I spent Rs.231 for Medicine today," the agent extracts the expense description, amount, and date, appends the entry to the spreadsheet, and returns a natural-language confirmation. The agent can also generate an on-demand categorized daily summary. The proposed system was implemented and tested with real conversational data, and the results demonstrate that the agent accurately parses free-form expense statements, updates the backend spreadsheet correctly, and produces coherent, human-readable summaries, thereby lowering the friction traditionally associated with manual expense tracking.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Multitask Bayesian Federated Learning for Multilingual Edge Translation
abstract: Multilingual edge translation must transfer knowledge across uneven language resources while controlling uncertainty and communication. Multitask Bayesian Federated Learning (MT-BayesFL) combines a shared six-layer Transformer encoder, target-specific decoders, lightweight adapters, and matrix-normal posteriors. The refined formulation separates Gaussian pooling from separable covariance approximation, preserves positive-definite sampling factors, and applies error feedback before sparse transmission. An adaptive projected-moment variant adds bounded reliability weights, between-client disagreement, and participation-dependent shrinkage. Reference-system results span eight English-to-target directions and five reported seeds. Low-resource macro BLEU is 26.0 versus 22.6 for FedMTL, with a 3.43-BLEU gain calculated from pairwise means. English-Swahili reaches 28.3 BLEU and expected calibration error 0.082. BLEU retention is 92.1% at 30% dropout; normalized retention over 0-40% dropout is 94.54%. Communication is 1.8 MB per round, 70.5% below the dense-upload ablation, and personalization improves by 4.5 BLEU on average. The parameter-efficient comparator remains stronger on English-Chinese. Numerical checks verify covariance and residual invariants; translation gains from the refinement remain unmeasured. These results support uncertainty-aware sharing for imbalanced multilingual clients, subject to configuration-matched evaluation.

title: Continuous-Time Cloth Dynamics with Physics-Informed Neural ODEs
abstract: We present ContinuousCloth, a continuous-time, physics-informed neural solver for deformable cloth dynamics that enforces a spring--mass ODE within a neural trajectory model. Unlike classical time-stepping simulators that return trajectories only on a discrete integration grid, ContinuousCloth supports querying at arbitrary timestamps and computing displacement, velocity, and acceleration via automatic differentiation. We evaluate ContinuousCloth along two dimensions. In a physics-only setting, ContinuousCloth achieves trajectory accuracy comparable to high-precision solvers across six diverse boundary-condition scenarios while reducing runtime by up to 17.4 times. When fused with sparse and noisy observations, the spring--mass ODE acts as a strong inductive bias for downstream tasks: interpolation and parameter estimation. That is, ContinuousCloth reduces interpolation error by 7.3 times over a data-only neural baseline in simulation and 2.4 times on real-world cloth sequences, and achieves 2.6 times lower parameter error than a differentiable-solver baseline under high-noise conditions, demonstrating consistent robustness under realistic measurement imperfections.

title: Ask Your Advisor: Learning When to Consult Stronger Models in Agentic Systems
abstract: To balance task performance and computational cost, agentic workflows can use a lower-cost model for execution and selectively consult a stronger model. In such executor-advisor systems, the executor decides when to seek advice, making escalation depend on self-assessment, although current language models struggle to detect where their own reasoning fails. The need for stronger reasoning emerges during execution and varies across workflow phases. We introduce ARIA, a meta-controller that learns when to consult by balancing task success against consultation cost. Our approach formulates consultation as a sequential resource-allocation problem. At workflow contact points, ARIA maps execution evidence to a compact state abstraction and selects SILENT or CONSULT, with action values learned by Monte Carlo control from cost-penalized outcomes. Across evaluated tasks of SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and $τ^2$-bench, ARIA recovers 44-81% of the executor-advisor success gap at less than half the advisor model's cost. ARIA achieves the best observed success-cost trade-off among ten other evaluated conditions, including routing and cascading methods, fixed and prompted consultation, and random placement at matched advice volume. The policies are compact and inspectable, with a single consultation-price parameter governing the success-cost trade-off without retraining either underlying model.

title: Robust Vision-Language Navigation with Awareness of Instruction-Execution Progress
abstract: In Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) tasks involving multi-step instructions as guidance, an agent must associate its observations with the relevant instruction content at each decision point. Most graph-based methods commonly match candidate trajectories with the entire instruction, allowing already executed content to interfere with subsequent decisions. Although instruction-execution progress provides a direct cue for separating executed and pending content, existing progress estimation approaches often rely on explicit progress supervision, sophisticated progress-learning stages, or costly online reasoning with LLMs. In this paper, we propose a robust VLN framework with Awareness of Instruction-Execution Progress (VLN-AIEP), which couples progress estimation with navigation decision-making. VLN-AIEP associates the visited trajectory with the instruction to suppress embeddings corresponding to executed content, and then matches candidate locations with the pending content. This coupling makes correct navigation decisions depend on accurate progress estimation, allowing the progress estimator to learn directly from navigation decision labels without explicit progress annotations. To support progress estimation, we construct a landmark-anchored trajectory representation that encodes the semantic labels and viewpoint-relative geometry of instruction-referred landmarks. These landmarks serve as spatial references for associating the visited trajectory with executed instruction content. Extensive experiments on R2R, RxR, CVDN, and R2R-CE demonstrate that the proposed method achieves favorable performance across multiple metrics.

title: From Generative AI to Hotel Brand Advocacy: A Proposed Research Framework
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly involved in travel planning and hotel choice, yet research has not fully explained how consumers move from evaluating an AI-generated recommendation to responding to the hotel brand being recommended. This paper develops an integrated research framework that connects GenAI-related perceptions with recommendation acceptance and hotel brand advocacy intention. The framework distinguishes two psychological routes. A motivational route links GenAI anthropomorphism with GenAI-evoked inspiration, whereas an evaluative route links recommendation credibility and relevance with trust in GenAI recommendations. Inspiration and trust are subsequently proposed to increase recommendation acceptance, which is further associated with advocacy intention toward the recommended hotel brand. The framework also proposes that lack-of-transparency anxiety weakens the positive effect of GenAI anthropomorphism on inspiration. The Stimulus - Organism - Response (S-O-R) framework provides the overall structure, while customer inspiration, affordance - actualization, fear-acquisition, and commitment - consistency perspectives explain specific relationships. Eight hypotheses are developed, together with a pathway for future empirical validation using a survey of GenAI users and partial least squares structural equation modeling. The framework extends GenAI hospitality research by connecting recommendation-level psychological responses with a downstream hotel-brand outcome.

title: Pick Aggregator: A Multimodel Ensemble of Machine Learning Pickers to Generate an Onshore–Offshore Seismic Catalog for Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands
abstract: Abstract Offshore seismic swarms north of Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands remain poorly characterized due to limited azimuthal coverage from the inland Puerto Rico Seismic Network (network code PR). Here, we integrate data from six U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) ocean-bottom seismometers (ZZ network, mid-2015 to mid-2016) with the PR network using a novel multimodel ensemble approach for machine learning (ML) phase picking, named pick aggregator. ML pickers have automated rapid seismic phase detection, but their performance degrades when applied to data that differ significantly from training datasets. Onshore–offshore experiments with sparse station coverage, complex instrumentation, and lower signal-to-noise ratios provide a challenge. The pick aggregator performs multidomain parallel computations on the SeisBench platform to catalog seismic phases across eight ML model combinations pretrained on ocean and land data. We then aggregate seismic picks identified by at least two models and associate them using a Gaussian Mixture Model Associator. The 1-yr ensemble ML catalog includes 10,948 events, composed of 55,704 P wave and 33,899 S wave picks, with mean probabilities of 0.65 and 0.64, respectively. The ZZ network substantially improves offshore azimuthal coverage and provides thousands of near-source seismic phases (25% of the P wave and 28% of the S wave picks). The relocated-ML catalog with >5.3 M added differential times includes 8025 events (115.8% increase compared with the relocated USGS catalog using the same stations). The relocated-ML catalog reveals an intense seismic swarm in the north-northwest direction southeast of the Main ridge at 20–40 km depth that aligns with the fast shear-wave polarization of previous studies, suggesting an incipient slab tear near 65.1° W. Seismicity depth variations along the strike indicate a steeper western segment with a wider depth range and a retreating eastern segment, supporting a differential rollback mechanism. Our multimodel ensemble approach mitigates inconsistencies among ML pickers pretrained on different datasets, enabling superior performance and robust phase detection in diverse tectonic environments with varying signal characteristics.

evidence.title: Pick Aggregator: A Multimodel Ensemble of Machine Learning Pickers to Generate an Onshore–Offshore Seismic Catalog for Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands
evidence.abstract: Abstract Offshore seismic swarms north of Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands remain poorly characterized due to limited azimuthal coverage from the inland Puerto Rico Seismic Network (network code PR). Here, we integrate data from six U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) ocean-bottom seismometers (ZZ network, mid-2015 to mid-2016) with the PR network using a novel multimodel ensemble approach for machine learning (ML) phase picking, named pick aggregator. ML pickers have automated rapid seismic phase detection, but their performance degrades when applied to data that differ significantly from training datasets. Onshore–offshore experiments with sparse station coverage, complex instrumentation, and lower signal-to-noise ratios provide a challenge. The pick aggregator performs multidomain parallel computations on the SeisBench platform to catalog seismic phases across eight ML model combinations pretrained on ocean and land data. We then aggregate seismic picks identified by at least two models and associate them using a Gaussian Mixture Model Associator. The 1-yr ensemble ML catalog includes 10,948 events, composed of 55,704 P wave and 33,899 S wave picks, with mean probabilities of 0.65 and 0.64, respectively. The ZZ network substantially improves offshore azimuthal coverage and provides thousands of near-source seismic phases (25% of the P wave and 28% of the S wave picks). The relocated-ML catalog with >5.3 M added differential times includes 8025 events (115.8% increase compared with the relocated USGS catalog using the same stations). The relocated-ML catalog reveals an intense seismic swarm in the north-northwest direction southeast of the Main ridge at 20–40 km depth that aligns with the fast shear-wave polarization of previous studies, suggesting an incipient slab tear near 65.1° W. Seismicity depth variations along the strike indicate a steeper western segment with a wider depth range and a retreating eastern segment, supporting a differential rollback mechanism. Our multimodel ensemble approach mitigates inconsistencies among ML pickers pretrained on different datasets, enabling superior performance and robust phase detection in diverse tectonic environments with varying signal characteristics.

title: A symmetry breaking swarm optimizer derived from the Landau theory of phase transitions
abstract: Supplementary code and data for the manuscript submitted to Scientific Reports. Contains the SBSO (symmetry breaking swarm optimizer) implementation, eleven comparison algorithms, benchmark drivers including the CEC2017 suite, statistical and robustness analyses, figure-generation scripts, and the complete numerical results (JSON and CSV) underlying all tables and figures in the manuscript.

title: Probability-based thresholding for guided perturbation sampling in XAI
abstract: Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) is a visual explainability model that is used in explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) systems to understand the decision behavior of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). LIME is a perturbation-based model; hence, it suffers from instability-of-explainability problems due to run-to-run variability in feature ranking. We have addressed this problem recently using a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm to guide perturbation sampling and propose an adaptive MCMC-LIME visual explainer. However, MCMC introduces new challenges that include slow convergence to target distribution and high autocorrelation between samples that may introduce uncertainty across complementary learning models. MCMC generally navigates in high-probability regions, leading to difficulties switching to other high-probability regions that are important contributors to stabilizing visual explainers. This paper proposes an improved MCMCLIME that can function effectively in the recently proposed Colony of AI framework, a specialized multi-agent AI system that integrates three complementary learner AI agents (fast, detailed, and organized). The improved MCMC-LIME introduces a probability-based thresholding to control guided perturbation sampling and stabilize MCMC-LIME across learner AI agents. An experiment is conducted using a Samoyed dog image from Oxford- IIIT Pet dataset with seven independent runs per model. It uses VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 models that are labeled as fast, detailed, and organized learner AI agents in colony of AI. Experimental results, evaluated using the Average Rank Similarity (ARS) scores and averaging across five independent ARS evaluations per model, show LIME achieves ARS scores of (0.92, 0.75, 0.83) for the three types of learner AI agents, respectively. Similarly, MCMC-LIME achieves (0.95, 0.80, 0.91) ARS scores. However, the improved MCMC-LIME leads to (0.98, 0.86, 0.98) ARS scores, respectively, indicating about 6.5%, 14.7%, and 18.1% improvement across learner AI agents from the original LIME explainer. As such, the probability-based thresholding guides perturbation sampling efficiently and improves performance of XAI.

title: Opto-electronic programmable activation function generation circuit for photonic computing
abstract: I propose and report an opto-electronic circuit for photonic computing, which generates various kinds of activation functions including tanh and rectified linear unit (ReLU) in response to the electric field of an input signal. The circuit is composed of a symmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI), a balanced photodetector (PD), and an MZI-based optical intensity modulator. When two coherent lightwaves (input and control signals) are input into the symmetric MZI, the optical output of the intensity modulator, which is driven with the electrical output of the balanced PD set after the symmetric MZI, produces various kinds of activation responses to the input signal by setting a diode and/or changing the amplitude and phase of the control signal.

title: Introduction to using symbolic regression for interpretable machine learning in healthcare
abstract: The past decade has seen machine learning play an increasingly important role in medicine. However, many of the state-of-the-art models being developed and deployed suffer from a lack of transparency, limiting integration into the clinical decision-making process and raising concerns about patient safety. Here we call attention to symbolic regression, a largely overlooked machine learning technique that aims to be both accurate and interpretable by learning readable mathematical models from data. In recent years, it has undergone rapid advancements with successful application to problems across a wide range of disciplines. In this perspective, we provide an approachable introduction to symbolic regression, highlight its strengths and limitations, and explore its potential applications in medicine.

title: STREGO: A Scalable Implementation of a Trust-Region Framework for Noisy Bayesian Optimization
abstract: TREGO, a trust-region Bayesian optimization (BO) method for expensive blackbox problems, has convergence guarantees, but only for exact function values. In high dimension, its performance tends to deteriorate. This paper asks whether a trust-region BO method can be extended to handle noisy evaluations while being competitive in high dimension. We first generalize TREGO into a trust-region framework for noisy BO and extend its convergence analysis to noisy function estimates that are sufficiently accurate with sufficiently high probability. We then propose STREGO, a scalable implementation of this framework. Its global phase selects a batch of candidates by solving a bi-objective problem on the posterior mean of a Gaussian process and the integrated variance reduction. Unlike the predictive variance, this second objective does not favor boundary points merely because they are far from the data. Its local phase minimizes the posterior mean of a second Gaussian process, trained only on points close to the incumbent. STREGO is compared with TREGO, TURBO, BAXUS and NSMA-BO on synthetic and real-world problems of dimension $4$ to $124$, with and without noise. It gives the best average results in every synthetic setting tested and the best or tied-best solution on four of the six real-world problems. An implementation of STREGO is available at https://github.com/Mayousk/STREGO.
